sentences.text: 1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injures sustained by her in the road traffic accident occurred on 30.07.2024.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 30.07.2024 at about 9.00 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Rajajinagar Traffic Police Station, in front of Bramhashree Grand Hotel, Laggere Pipeline underpass Outer Ring road, when the accused riding the offending Bajaj Pulsar Motor Cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-JW-3658 along with Petitioner as pillion 3 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 rider and he drove the same from Summanahalli towards Dr. Rajkumar Samadhi in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and jumped the road humps and lost his control and fall on the road
, as a result, the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on her right leg knee.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Vijayanagar Hospital, Bengaluru wherein she was treated as inpatient from 30.07.2024 to 08.08.2024 and undergone surgery.

She has spent Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical expenditure and other incidental charges.
In this regard the Petitioner has lodged complaint before the Rajajinagar Traffic police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.143/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

3. Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and she was aged about 27 years and she was an employee in Metro (BMRCL) and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged 4 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 accident he lost her income and future prospective life, happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the rider of the offending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02- JW-3658.
Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.
4. In response to the notice, the Respondent No.1 is placed exparte and the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through their counsel and filed the written statement.

sentences.text: On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint, on 31.07.2024, the informant has showed the place of incident to the police.
The police have conducted the detailed spot mahazar in the presence of panch witnesses and prepared Ex.P.4/Spot Sketch 19.
Admittedly, the accused is the rider of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, Petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed that the said accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged 13 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 accident occurred due to no fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, he was riding slowly and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot mahazar, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that,
the rider of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 is corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle along with Petitioner as pillion rider in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to 14 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 endanger human life and caused accident, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P3/Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4/Spot sketch, Ex.P8/Wound Certificate and Ex.P-9/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P8/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent women/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the 15 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 accused/rider of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that her earning was about Rs.30,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established her income, she is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

22. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident she was aged about 27 years and she relied 16 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 on the Ex.P.12/Adhar Card, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 30.11.1997 and this accident was took place on 30.07.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 26 years 8 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 26 years.
23. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider/accused.

In the instance case the petitioner claimed that she was an employee in Metro (BMRCL) and earning sum of Rs.30,000/-
p.m.
But she has not produced single piece of document to prove her actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the Petitioner is taken at Rs.15,750/-.
24.

In the chief examination of PW-3/Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained open fracture right proximal tibia and she underwent open reduction internal fixation with plate and screws and now the Petitioner complaints of pain 17 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 and weakness in the right leg unable to sit down squat sit cross leg and on examination the Petitioner has wasting of right thigh and calf muscle restricted right knee movement.

Further deposed that the recent X-ray of the right leg shows united fracture with implant in situ and the Petitioner has sustained physical disability of the right lower limb at 40% and whole body disability at 13% and the Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of the implant the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
PW-3 has produced Ex.P.19/Clinical report and Ex.P.20/X-ray Film.
In the Cross examination of PW.3/doctor by the counsel for Respondent No.2 he has deposed that he has not a treated doctor of the Petitioner.

Prior to assessing the disability he has not taken advice from the treated doctor and even he has not tried to contact the treated doctor and he has not gone through the case sheet and old X-ray film.
The Petitioner has sustained fracture of proximal tibia.
The right leg tibia and fibula are the weight bearing bones.
Now fracture is united and the implants are therein and it is right time to remove the implants.
As the fractures are united she can walk without the support of others.
He do not know about the job of the Petitioner.
The Petitioner can do sitting work.
He has 18 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 assessed the physical disability of the Petitioner.
He has not given estimation certificate for the future medical expenditure.
Further he has denied that Rs.60,000/- is not required for the future medical expenditure.
Further he has denied that as he has not a treated doctor, he is not a right person to assess the disability of the Petitioner.
Further he denied that in order to help the petitioner he has assessed disability on the higher side and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

sentences.text: As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as employee of metro, while doing her work the petitioner has to sit and stand for long time and she has to sit down, squat sit cross leg she has to use her legs to walk, climb staircases and lift the weights and to do her regular routine activities.
But due to injuries sustained in the alleged accident, she is not in a position to do work as earlier.
The doctor stated that the Petitioner has sustained physical disability of the right lower limb at 40% and whole body disability at 13%.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 13% to the whole body.
With regard to the quantum, age of the petitioner is considered as 26 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,750/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 17 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 13%.

On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs. 15,750/- X 12 X 17 X 13/100) = Rs.4,17,690/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.4,17,690/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.

27. In the alleged accident, the petitioner has sustained open fracture right proximal tibia and she underwent open reduction internal fixation with plate and screws, which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.

28. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment at Vijayanagar Hospital wherein she was taken treatment as an inpatient from 30.07.2024 to 08.08.2024, i.e., for 9 days.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to 20 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 award Rs.45,000/- (Rs.5,000/- X 9 days) under head of special diet and conveyance.
29. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in her day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
30. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.94,500/- (Rs.15,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
31. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical bills, towards medical expenses as per Ex.P.13 for an amount of Rs.1,93,400/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,93,400/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.
32. In the evidence affidavit of PW-3/doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.60,000/-.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.60,000/-
compensation under the head future medical expenses.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Respondent No.2 admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident 8 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 occurred due to the negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the rider of the offending vehicle, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtain the compensation Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that she was an employee in Metro (BMRCL) and earning sum of Rs.30,000/-
p.m.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
The accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed that the said accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged 13 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 accident occurred due to no fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, he was riding slowly and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot mahazar, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that,
the rider of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 is corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle along with Petitioner as pillion rider in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to 14 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 endanger human life and caused accident, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P8/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent women/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the 15 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.6514/2024 accused/rider of the offending vehicle.
